_comment: Methodology checklists for learning offensive security on INTENTIONALLY-VULNERABLE practice labs (HackTheBox, TryHackMe, your own VMs). These are educational study guides, not automation.

phases.name: Enumeration
steps: Record the target IP and scope; confirm it is a practice lab.
Full TCP port discovery, then service/version enumeration on open ports.
Enumerate each service methodically (web, SMB, FTP, DNS, etc.).
Note software names and versions for later CVE research.

phases.name: Research
steps: Look up known vulnerabilities for identified versions (offline notes / CVE DBs).
Read official docs and public write-ups for the technology.
Map which findings are most promising and why.

phases.name: Foothold (lab only)
steps: Understand the vulnerability class before attempting anything.
Document the intended approach and expected result.
Capture evidence: what worked, what didn't, and lessons learned.

phases.name: Post & Reporting
steps: Enumerate the local system for privilege-escalation learning opportunities.
Write up the full path clearly enough to reproduce it.
Note the defensive lesson: how would a blue team detect/prevent this?

phases.name: Mapping
steps: Identify the stack (server, framework, language) from headers and behavior.
Enumerate directories/endpoints; review robots.txt and source comments.
Catalogue inputs: forms, params, headers, cookies.

phases.name: Analysis
steps: Reason about each OWASP Top 10 category against observed inputs.
Check authentication/session handling logic.
Review any file upload / template / deserialization surfaces.

phases.name: Defensive lesson
steps: For each finding, note the correct fix (validation, encoding, authz).
Write a detection idea (WAF rule, log signature).

phases.name: Enumeration
steps: Enumerate shares and null-session exposure.
Identify OS build and SMB dialect/version.
List users/groups where the lab exposes them.

phases.name: Research
steps: Match the SMB/OS version to known advisories in your notes.
Understand the vulnerability before proceeding.

phases.name: Defensive lesson
steps: Note SMB signing, patch level, and segmentation as mitigations.
Sketch a detection for anomalous SMB access.

redteam.title: Red-team / adversary-emulation study plan (ATT&CK, labs only)
redteam._note: A STUDY checklist mapped to MITRE ATT&CK for learning on intentionally-vulnerable labs you own or are authorized to use. For every offensive concept, record the matching BLUE-TEAM detection and mitigation - understanding both sides is the point.

phases.name: Reconnaissance (TA0043)
steps: Study how service/version enumeration reveals attack surface (T1595, T1046).
Record which recon activity is noisy and how a defender would see it.
Note the detection: unusual scan volume, uncommon user-agents.

phases.name: Initial Access (TA0001)
steps: Understand the vulnerability class behind the lab's entry point (T1190, T1566).
Document the root cause, not just the trigger.
Note the mitigation: patching, input validation, MFA, email filtering.

phases.name: Execution & Persistence (TA0002 / TA0003)
steps: Learn how code execution maps to logs (T1059) and what artifacts it leaves.
Study common persistence mechanisms and where they register (T1053, T1543).
Note the detection: process/command-line logging, autoload auditing.

phases.name: Privilege Escalation (TA0004)
steps: Enumerate misconfigurations that enable escalation on the lab host (T1068, T1548).
Explain WHY each works at the OS level.
Note the mitigation: least privilege, patching, sudo/UAC hardening.

phases.name: Lateral Movement & Exfil (TA0008 / TA0010)
steps: Study how credentials/sessions enable movement in the lab network (T1021, T1550).
Understand how data staging/exfiltration looks on the wire (T1041).
Note the detection: segmentation, egress monitoring, anomalous auth.

phases.name: Report & Blue-team feedback
steps: Write a clear, reproducible path from entry to objective.
For each step, pair it with an outcats detection rule or hardening check.
Propose concrete fixes an owner could apply to close the path.
